subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Should repeated authenticated ACP `loadSession` replay requests be treated as an in-scope security boundary, reliability hardening only, or no actionable issue under the trusted-operator model?
rationale: Current source disproves the reported arbitrary recursive-filter path, but only a security owner should decide whether bounded replay flooding by an authenticated local ACP client merits separate hardening.

options.title: Close as invalid security report
options.body: Close because current main has no client-defined filter AST and the remaining authenticated replay behavior does not cross the documented trusted-operator boundary.

options.title: Narrow to reliability hardening
options.body: Retain or replace this issue with a scoped task to benchmark repeated `loadSession` calls and add a translator-level concurrency or replay-work budget only if measurable impact exists.

options.title: Request a current PoC
options.body: Keep the issue pending until the reporter supplies an exact current SHA, invocation sequence, resource measurements, and the security boundary crossed.

recommendation.title: Close as invalid security report
recommendation.body: Close because current main has no client-defined filter AST and the remaining authenticated replay behavior does not cross the documented trusted-operator boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently maintained the ACP session-load replay behavior at the center of the remaining question.
